@graph.name: Business-Wrap
@graph.description: Free, open-source bilingual document studio. 17 document types for business analysts and testers (SRS, BRD, FRS, test plan, test cases, user manual, UAT sign-off, release notes and more), plus a requirements document built from a process model or a live e-service, edited on the page that prints and exported to PDF and DOCX.
@graph.applicationSubCategory: Document studio for business analysts and testers
@graph.softwareRequirements: Node.js 20 or newer, Chrome or Edge, Python with uv for DOCX
featureList: A start page and 17 document types (SRS, BRD, FRS, RTM, process flow, test plan, test cases, defect report, user manual, UAT sign-off, release notes, ToR, change request, minutes, business case, TOT guide), each in Arabic and English
Harvest from a process model (BPMN, draw.io, YAML) or a crawl of the live service, and merge both
One HTML editor that is the print layout; every edit recorded and undoable
Arabic right to left and English left to right, both first-class
Editable workflow diagrams with Mermaid import and export
PDF and DOCX export with fonts embedded as real text
Six template packs plus custom packs
Update from inside the editor, with rollback
Claude Code plugin and a local MCP server

mainEntity.name: Which documents can I make with Business-Wrap?

acceptedAnswer.text: 17 types: blank, SRS, BRD, FRS, RTM, process flow, test plan, test cases, defect report, user manual, UAT sign-off, release notes, ToR, change request, minutes, business case and a TOT guide. Each exports PDF and DOCX in Arabic and English.
Yes. It is open source under the MIT licence. There is no paid plan and no account.

mainEntity.name: Does my document leave my computer?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The editor, PDF printing and DOCX building run locally. The one automatic request is the update check, at most once a day, to the public GitHub release list. Webhooks send only to an address you set.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Claude to use it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The editor and the command line work on their own. The Claude Code plugin and the MCP server are optional ways in.

mainEntity.name: Which inputs and outputs does it support?

acceptedAnswer.text: In: a process model (BPMN, draw.io, YAML) or a crawl of a live service. Out: PDF, DOCX, an edits JSON file, a design pack, and the editor saved as HTML.
